story.title: Manhunt Underway After Deadly Attack at Berlin Pride Event
story.summary: A manhunt is ongoing for a 21-year-old suspect following a deadly attack near Berlin's Pride festival, which left one person dead and at least 16 injured. Authorities suspect the incident, involving a van ramming and subsequent stabbings, to be an act of Islamist terrorism. The suspect has been identified and is believed to have connections to extremist groups.

explore_lenses.label: Why does an attack near Pride carry wider stakes?
explore_lenses.title: A test of safety and civic freedom
explore_lenses.summary: The attack was near, rather than on, the festival route, but it disrupted one of Europe’s largest LGBTQ+ gatherings and prompted officials and community representatives to frame it as an attack on an open, pluralistic public life.

claims.text: Police said the vehicle struck people in Tiergarten, a few hundred meters from the Pride closing event; the parade’s final festivities were called off shortly afterward.
LSVD+ official Andre Lehmann said the suspected attack "hits the heart of the queer community," while Berlin’s LGBTQ affairs commissioner Alfonso Pantisano said many people were afraid but not alone.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz characterized the violence as intended to divide society and said the government would defend openness and freedom; that is the government’s political framing, not a judicial finding on motive.

explore_lenses.label: What is confirmed about the suspect and attack?
explore_lenses.title: The case is still at the manhunt stage
explore_lenses.summary: Authorities have named a 21-year-old suspect and described a vehicle assault followed by stabbings, but the public evidence remains preliminary while the suspect is at large.

claims.text: Berlin police and prosecutors said Abdul B., 21, is suspected of injuring several people with a vehicle around 10 p.m. on July 25 in Tiergarten; they also said one or more people left the vehicle and that several people were wounded with stabbing weapons.

Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said authorities saw indications of an Islamist terrorist attack and described the suspect as previously known for criminality, radicalization, and links to the Islamist scene. Those are official allegations and assessments, not findings tested in court.

The injury count was revised upward during the response: Berlin’s city information page reported one woman killed and 29 others injured, while the police appeal initially described multiple injuries, including life-threatening ones.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next for Berlin and other events?
explore_lenses.title: Search, victim support, and a security review
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate priorities are locating the suspect, collecting public evidence, and supporting victims. Officials have also signaled that security planning for upcoming major events may be reassessed.

claims.text: Berlin police asked witnesses to upload their own photos and videos, and warned the public not to approach the suspect because he may be armed and dangerous.
Police searched an apartment in Schöneberg early on July 26 but did not find the suspect, according to the Associated Press.
Forecast: Dobrindt said security arrangements for other large German events, including Pride events, would be reviewed and strengthened if necessary; he said copycat crimes could not be ruled out.
A memorial drew hundreds of people in Berlin, while organizers canceled some associated events and replaced them with a vigil, showing an immediate community response alongside the investigation.

related_stories.title: David Jonsson Cast as New Black Panther at Comic-Con 2026
related_stories.summary: Ryan Coogler announced that David Jonsson will take on the role of the new Black Panther during Comic-Con 2026. This casting marks a significant development for the franchise, as Jonsson is set to portray T'Challa's son in the upcoming third film.

related_stories.title: Flavio Bolsonaro Officially Launches Presidential Campaign in Brazil
related_stories.summary: Flavio Bolsonaro, a Brazilian senator and son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, has officially launched his presidential campaign to challenge incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in the upcoming October elections. He received endorsements from Argentine President Javier Milei and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, along with a message from his jailed father.

related_stories.title: Ebola Outbreak in DR Congo Exceeds 3,000 Cases Amid Health Worker Strike
related_stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo has reported over 3,000 confirmed cases of Ebola, marking the fastest-growing outbreak in history. This announcement coincides with a strike by approximately 100 health workers at an Ebola treatment center in Bunia, the outbreak's epicenter.

related_stories.title: Troy Jackson Secures Democratic Nomination for U.S. Senate in Maine
related_stories.summary: Troy Jackson, a former state lawmaker and logger, has been chosen as the Democratic nominee for the U.S. Senate in Maine. He will challenge incumbent Republican Senator Susan Collins in the upcoming November election. Jackson replaces Graham Platner, who initially won the Democratic primary in June.
